ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is an isosceles triangle, with the vertex at the top and the base horizontal, and a vertical altitude line from the vertex to the base is drawn in the center. Several horizontal lines divide the triangle into horizontal strips of equal height; in each horizontal strip, the two sides to the left and right of the central altitude line are respectively colored white and gray, and the left and right colors are opposite. Reasoning: Because the triangle is an isosceles triangle, this vertical altitude line in the figure is also the axis of symmetry, so it will bisect any horizontal secant line. Thus each horizontal strip is divided by the altitude line into two parts with equal areas on the left and right. Also because in each strip the left and right two parts are one white and one gray, the white area of each strip exactly accounts for half of the area of that strip. Adding all the strips together, the white area of the whole triangle also accounts for half of the total area.

raw_record.question_text: The diagram shows an isosceles triangle, where the height is marked and its area is split up into equally wide white and grey stripes. Which fraction of the area of the triangle is white?

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as an isosceles triangle with a vertical marked height that is also the axis of symmetry. The horizontal lines divide the triangle into equally tall stripe bands, and in each band the two pieces on opposite sides of the height have opposite colors: one white and one grey. Since the triangle is isosceles, the height bisects every horizontal cross-section, so within each horizontal band the left and right portions have equal area. Therefore each band is exactly half white and half grey. Adding over all bands gives white area equal to half the total triangle area, so the required fraction is 1/2.

method.method_draft: View the marked height as a mirror line. Reflect the entire triangle across this vertical height. Because the triangle is isosceles, the reflected triangle coincides with the original triangle. From the image, the coloring is complementary across the height: each white stripe segment on one side reflects to a grey segment of the same size on the other side, and each grey segment reflects to a white one. Reflection preserves area, so it gives an area-preserving one-to-one match between all white regions and all grey regions. Hence the white and grey areas are equal, and the white fraction of the whole triangle is 1/2.
